name: Which Street Would You Prefer to Walk On? (London, SP-Scheme)
description:
Method replication: same task, scales and design as the paper; the images are not the paper's stimuli (168 new Google Street View images of Greater London). Participants see two London street views side by side and answer the paper's single question, "On which street would you prefer to walk?", by clicking one image or "Not comparable"; 30 pairs per participant, then three background questions (London-based, gender, how often they walk). Each street view looks at the building fronts, perpendicular to the street, as in the paper. The paper aggregates the binary choices into image-level preference scores, removes raters who chose one side more than 90% of the time, checks agreement on repeated pairs across groups (London-based or not, female or male, walking at least twice a week or not), and trains a deep learning model to map preference across London.

Original study: Muller, Gemmell, Choudhury, Nathvani, Metzler, Bennett, Denton, Flaxman & Ezzati (2022), "City-Wide Perceptions of Neighbourhood Quality using Street View Images", arXiv:2211.12139. About 25,000 Google Street View images from 2018, sampled on the London street network and stratified by k-means clusters of image features; 207 raters (personal networks and Amazon Mechanical Turk) gave 37,966 pairwise ratings in April–June 2022.

Differences from the original study: (1) 168 images from random points within about 22 km of central London, one view per point to a randomly chosen side, 2018 captures where available (123 of 168) and the latest capture otherwise; (2) pairs are drawn at random from the whole set, without the paper's weighting towards pairs within the same image cluster; (3) a fixed 30 pairs per participant instead of open-ended play (the paper's raters averaged 132 images); (4) the background questions are written for this template from the groups the paper compares; the paper's full demographic form is not given. Images: © Google Street View.
author: Muller, E., Gemmell, E., Choudhury, I., Nathvani, R., Metzler, A. B., Bennett, J., Denton, E., Flaxman, S., & Ezzati, M.
